name: One-nation conservatism
summary: One-nation conservatism is the British paternalist strand of Toryism that defends established institutions such as the Crown and Church while holding that the privileged owe duties to the poor. It sees society as an organic, hierarchical whole that should be reconciled across classes through social reform and gradual change rather than class conflict or doctrinaire markets. In practice it accepted the post-war welfare state and mixed economy and is pragmatic rather than ideological.
scope: Disraelian Tory democracy (Coningsby, Sybil, the 1872 Crystal Palace speech) as carried on by Baldwin, Chamberlain, Butler and Macmillan in the post-war consensus and by later self-described one-nation Tories. Excludes the New Right and Thatcherite free-market strand, and non-British conservatisms. Several modern issues were never addressed and are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Benjamin Disraeli
keyFigures.role: Originator of the 'two nations' idea and Tory democracy, in Sybil and as Conservative prime minister.

keyFigures.name: Rab Butler
keyFigures.role: Architect of the post-war 'new conservatism' and the Industrial Charter.

sources.usedFor: 1947 Conservative acceptance of a mixed economy and workers' rights, opposition to protectionism and Labour planning.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Post-war one-nation Conservatives accepted the NHS and welfare state as part of the consensus, treating basic provision as an obligation of a united society.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a classic one-nation question; paternalists favour protecting workers, but pragmatic Tories worried about business costs and were split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: One-nationers accepted markets and private enterprise but explicitly rejected the New Right claim that markets beat state action across the board; adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: The Industrial Charter accepted a mixed economy and consensus-era nationalisations but criticised Labour planning; one-nationers tolerated rather than advocated public ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Noblesse oblige asks the privileged to share, mainly through duty and charity; whether this meant significantly higher taxes is not settled and varied by era.

unions-good.rationale: Disraeli's 1875 Acts protected collective action and the Industrial Charter pledged to safeguard workers' rights, so unions were seen as a legitimate partner in class reconciliation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Conservatives treat property as part of the inherited order, though one-nationers qualify it with duties to those below.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Paternalist state protection of the people implies some regulation, but one-nation Tories also defended business and disliked bloated controls; no settled line.

cut-welfare.rationale: One-nationism arose to give social support; the New Right's attack on welfare dependency is documented as the position it opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Class harmony within the existing order rather than transferring ownership to workers; the idea is socialist and not part of Tory paternalism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented one-nation position; authority-minded conservatism leans yes while civil-liberties Tories dissent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist, authority-oriented conservatism; mainstream one-nation Tories did not push drug legalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed; pragmatic Tories supported public-order laws but some prize free speech, so adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: One-nationism works through parliament, institutions and compromise, not leaders bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: One-nation conservatism values inherited institutions and a paternal state that supports the population, which clearly rules out treating the state as harmful; no source addresses anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from British Tory acceptance of strict gun control after the 1980s; not a stated one-nation tenet.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order, authority and the maintenance of institutions and empire lead conservatives to back the forces of the state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from traditional morality; most one-nationers were socially cautious.

rehabilitation.rationale: Paternalist concern for the poor suggests sympathy, but Tories also stress order and punishment; no documented one-nation line.

traditional-family.rationale: Conservatives see family, property and religion as foundations of social order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Cameron-era one-nationers legalised it while older and religious Tories opposed; the strand is genuinely split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Traditionally a matter of conscience in the Conservative Party; one-nationers divided between religious caution and pragmatic reform.

more-religion-public.rationale: Disraeli defended the Church as an institution of the nation and conservatives see religion as a key tradition, though one-nationism is not theocratic.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Never addressed historically; paternalist duty to the disadvantaged is offset by distrust of engineered social redesign.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from conservative belief in traditional social roles and distrust of abstract theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Maintaining national institutions and traditions is the first of Disraeli's three great objects.

gradual-change.rationale: Society is seen as an organism that should develop naturally; reform is piecemeal and respects institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a defining one-nation issue; Powellite restrictionists and pragmatic moderates both claim the Tory tradition.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Disraeli's national and imperial emphasis suggests wariness of supranational bodies, though post-war Tories supported the UN framework.

free-trade.rationale: The Industrial Charter turned against protection while Disraeli backed an imperial tariff, so the tradition is split on free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Disraeli contrasted national and imperial greatness with cosmopolitan Liberalism, putting country first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Never addressed directly; imperial power and moral considerations on one side, pragmatic caution on the other.

open-borders.rationale: A tradition of nation, institutions and patriotism rejects open borders as incompatible with national community.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: one-nationers accepted Keynesian growth economics and had no tradition of de-growth, though stewardship ideas exist.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; pragmatic and Burkean stewardship favours action but gradualism and cost caution temper it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Conservative scepticism about human perfectibility counters optimism about technology; no stated position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from pragmatic post-war acceptance of state-backed energy programmes; not a stated tenet.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement was motivated by preventing revolution through reform, and conservatives oppose revolutionary change.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authority and hierarchy favour elite judgment, but Tory democracy courted the electorate; adherents are split.

central-planning.rationale: One-nation Tories accepted Keynesian management but criticised Labour's planning as producing bloat and restrictions.

socialized-markets.rationale: Accepts markets and a mixed economy but ownership by workers or the state is not a stated aim.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred from defence of landed property and inheritance; a Georgist single tax is outside the tradition.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Burke-derived conservatism ties liberty to inheritance, so heavy death duties are disliked.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; Butler's new conservatism targeted welfare at those in need and encouraged self-reliance.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Disraeli backed an imperial tariff while the Industrial Charter opposed protectionism; adherents were split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Interwar Chamberlain and Baldwin intervened while the Charter sought incentives over direction; no consensus.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Conservative stress on property and a stable social order, with Tory reformers wanting broad participation in it; loosely inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Socialist abolition of wages contradicts class reconciliation within the existing order.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Pragmatic institutionalism and acceptance of Keynesian management oppose abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Cooperation between employers and workers is valued, but formal state-recognised price-setting bodies are not a one-nation tenet.

one-party-rule.rationale: One-nation conservatism developed within British parliamentary competition and accepts alternation in office, which excludes single-party rule; the sources do not discuss it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Disraeli named maintaining the institutions of the country, especially the monarchy, as the first Tory object.

democracy-best.rationale: Tory democracy accepted the enlarged franchise, though hierarchy and doubts about majority rule temper enthusiasm.

direct-votes.rationale: Conservative preference for representative institutions over majoritarian plebiscites.

workers-councils.rationale: Socialist-derived structures rejected in favour of parliament and established institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Disraeli opposed disintegration of the empire; Unionist tradition values national unity.

natural-rulers.rationale: Disraeli viewed society as naturally hierarchical with those on top owing duties; the premise is accepted with obligation attached.

political-violence-never.rationale: Concerned with stability and order, though some force is accepted for state authority.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred; imperial pride existed but one-nationism's emphasis was on social stability.

separate-church-state.rationale: Defended an established Church as national institution; strict separation is opposed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is valued as tradition but one-nationism is pragmatic, not theocratic.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Paternalist state obligations and institutional trust rule out privatised justice and defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence of empire and national greatness imply a strong military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: One-nation means class unity within a nation, not ethnic homogeneity; Disraeli's empire was multi-ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class reconciliation and mutual obligation reject class conflict as the engine of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy is accepted as natural; reducing hardship is not equalising outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred; imperial-era Tory outlook was paternalist rather than devolving authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Disraeli championed the empire; modern one-nationers are pragmatic but reject reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: National and imperial focus does not extend to civilizational political unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Disraeli faulted Liberals as selfish individualists; the doctrine stresses mutual duty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Mutual obligation and noblesse oblige are core; conservatism leans toward authority.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No stated position; stewardship sentiment is present but not defining.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; Tory social traditionalism and pragmatism disfavour state population control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Sybil laments industrial inequality but seeks to reform, not repudiate, industrial society.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Opposed to disrupting existing institutions; change should be gradual.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from conservative caution and traditionalism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from reliance on human judgment, accountability and tradition.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; civil-liberty and security instincts conflict.

restore-past-order.rationale: Disraeli romanticised the older order, but one-nationism accepts evolving adaptation rather than restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: One-nationism presents itself as pragmatic and non-ideological, judging policies by their effect on stability.

direct-action.rationale: Works through parliament and institutions; direct action is outside the tradition.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not a conservative formulation; change should be gradual yet no stated link of means and ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contrary to organic, evolved, civilised society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchy and ordered society reject the idea.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Safety-net provision exists but distribution by need as the general principle is socialist.

production-for-use.rationale: Accepts private enterprise and profit incentives.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Class reconciliation denies that profit is exploitation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Empire is defended and the thesis is Marxist-Leninist.

taxation-theft.rationale: Paternalist state support requires taxation as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Paternalism holds that the state promotes welfare and morality, not just prevents harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Conservatives stress duties, community and institutions rather than individual rights alone.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; patriotism supports it in emergencies while peacetime views were split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Tory democracy values political participation and rejects the exit logic of the New Right.

state-as-business.rationale: Mutual obligation and paternalism are distinct from commercial customer logic.

positive-liberty.rationale: Support for social reform and material support for the poor accords with this idea, though not framed in those terms.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a one-nation claim; more a populist-right trope.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Race and ability are never discussed; the tradition's focus is class duty, and rejection is assumed.

organic-representation.rationale: Organic society appeals but representation is through parties in parliament in practice.

total-state.rationale: Opposes engineered society and totalising state; conservatism distrusts rational planning.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Disraeli championed imperial expansion, but modern one-nationers do not seek territory.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule through parliamentary institutions, not feudal oaths, though Disraeli romanticised the feudal ideal.

bound-labor.rationale: Disraeli sympathised with the poor and opposed the poor's degradation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Particularist scepticism but not relativism about truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Conservatives vary; Burkean particularism sits against religious natural-law belief.

single-common-good.rationale: Class balance suggests national harmony over competing interest, yet pragmatism accepts compromise among groups.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Disraeli's Jewish ancestry did not make it a doctrine.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; inferred pragmatic scepticism about engineered cultural revival.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Class cooperation, not worker control, is the aim.

school-vouchers.rationale: The New Right's market mechanism is not one-nation, though Butler's reforms preserved a mix.

economic-freedom.rationale: One-nationers accept markets but not the New Right claim that political liberty depends on them.

rule-by-example.rationale: Noblesse oblige holds elites must lead by honourable example, though laws still apply.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not a stated tenet; Disraeli prioritised empire over self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; imperial Tory tradition favours independence of action but post-war moderates supported the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Conservatism distrusts unchecked reason and values religion and tradition.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; mutual obligation within the nation but views vary.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Butler's updated conservatism stressed self-reliance and aid for those in need, while Disraeli's tradition resisted harsh poor-law conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: Reconciling employers and workers rather than letting them become opposed nations is the founding idea.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Western imperial and Atlanticist orientation.

workers-nation.rationale: The working class is meant to be integrated into the nation rather than organised internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Hierarchy supports traditional roles in older sources, modern one-nationers reject legal distinction.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is never discussed; rejection is assumed because the tradition accepts a market economy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Segregation law is never discussed; rejection is assumed from the one-nation theme of social unity.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Denies the Marxist view and sees the state as serving all classes.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: National tradition favours integration but is not clearly stated; adherents divided.

elite-replacement.rationale: The sources never discuss immigration conspiracies; rejection is assumed from the tradition's mainstream parliamentary character.

proportional-representation.rationale: Tories, as defenders of the constitution, preferred first-past-the-post.

national-mission.rationale: Disraeli emphasised imperial moral greatness, but modern one-nationers do not export government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Conservatism tends to deny systematic male advantage as structural oppression.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The tradition is built on a responsible governing elite.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is never discussed; rejection is assumed from the tradition's humanitarian social reformism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; state authority versus rule of law.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Directly opposed to the paternalist state and social protection.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mixed marriage is never discussed; rejection is assumed from the tradition's theme of national unity across classes.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Disraeli's concern for the poor and common humanity underlies the reforms, though hierarchy is accepted.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This Marxist debate is never discussed by one-nation conservatives; disagreement is assumed from their anti-socialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Disraeli championed the empire and settler colonies.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; Britain has no such religious personal-law question, so no position can be inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred; the Church of England is tolerant.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cow protection is never discussed; rejection is assumed because it has no place in British Tory politics.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion is seen as a key tradition.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist doctrine is never discussed; disagreement is assumed from the tradition's rejection of socialism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Tory democracy accepted mass franchise as legitimating government.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Disraeli attacked morbid competition (Sybil) and sought cooperation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; a constitution-defending instinct pulls one way and liberal tolerance the other.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine opposite to this tradition.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Concern for the condition of the people is one of the three objects.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Thatcher-era policy opposed by some one-nationers; split.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Disraeli's 1875 Acts protected peaceful picketing while later Conservative governments restricted strikes, so the tradition is divided.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Disraeli blamed social institutions and inequality.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not a one-nation claim; Disraeli's imperial vision multi-ethnic.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is never discussed; rejection is assumed from the tradition's belief in a responsible governing elite.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Wartime acceptance, but not a tenet.

party-commands-army.rationale: Incompatible with constitutional monarchy and parliament.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; cautious conservatism and pragmatic moderation point in opposite directions.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: MPs' pay is never discussed; rejection is assumed from the tradition's acceptance of a governing elite.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parliamentary party discipline exists in practice; no stated position.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional monarchy has ministers responsible to parliament.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Supports the established episcopal Church of England.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Paternalism concerned for morals, but censorship not stated.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Imperial and national power orientation favours alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The sources do not discuss rental housing; one-nation Tories promoted home ownership but are assumed not to ban renting.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Disraeli romanticised the old rural order.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; no stated position for a British doctrine and none inferable.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Disraeli held imperial England had higher national character.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; traditionalists object while pragmatic modernisers accept it, so adherents split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Pragmatic establishment unlikely to back it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; British law mixes descent and territory and the doctrine takes no side.

minority-language-support.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; unionist uniformity and pragmatic accommodation both have Tory advocates.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; support for religion is offset by insistence on a common law for all.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conservatives value custom and conformity to tradition.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not a stated view; Disraeli stressed political and imperial ties, with no claim that independence requires remaking property.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Duty to poor is domestic; no stated global duty.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; national attachment to territory is offset by pragmatic compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property carries duties to others per the noblesse oblige principle.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; caution accords but no stated position.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; a legalist stance suggests agreement but no one-nation text says so.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; pragmatic autonomy arrangements fit the tradition but are not stated.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine kingship is never discussed; rejection is assumed because the British constitutional monarchy makes no such claim.

decide-locally.rationale: Organic society values local institutions, but Tory paternalism and the national Crown and parliament favour central action; no stated position.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state is expected to use authority for order and empire; an absolutist non-aggression rule is a libertarian doctrine.

character-from-environment.rationale: Disraeli's Sybil blames the squalor and degradation of the poor on their conditions, but organic conservatism also stresses inherited character; inferred as a mild environmentalism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Tory defence of the Crown, Parliament and established institutions rests on constitutional, law-bound rule, so rulers are not above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the pragmatic, domestic social-reform focus that resources go to problems at home rather than a civilizational space goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Disraeli defended the balance of Crown, Lords and Commons and an aristocracy leading a broad popular franchise, the classic mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Conservatives honour the Crown and institutions rather than party leaders, and treat prime ministers as officeholders; mass leader worship is foreign to the tradition.

equal-parenting.rationale: Never addressed; paternalist family conservatism and fairness to fathers pull in different directions, so adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Class reconciliation across Disraeli's "two nations" is the tradition's defining aim, which is incompatible with this Maoist thesis; no source addresses it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Conservatism defends property and gradual change, and one-nation Tories sought reform of conditions, not seizing estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; no stance can be sourced.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Tory national principle concerns the nation and empire, not claims on foreigners based on nationality; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Defends the established church but modern one-nation Tories accept tolerance; inferred and low-confidence.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative respect for liberty and moderate, pragmatic politics.

common-currency.rationale: Tories prized national sovereignty and institutions such as the pound; inferred, though Macmillan sought European entry.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The national principle is tied to the nation under its Crown, not to kinship across borders; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Disraeli stressed national unity under the Crown and shared institutions; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; one-nation Tories valued unity and tolerance and had no clear stance.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Disraeli attacked class-based division in Sybil, and conservatives see history as shaped by institutions and tradition, not material change alone; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Pragmatic mixed-economy Tories accepted some regulation, but there is no documented stance on cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: Pragmatic and paternalist, with no sourced stance on bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty and respect for established institutions pull in opposite directions; adherents are split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Society is seen as an organic hierarchy, so quota rules are unlikely; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Industrial Charter opposed protectionism and planning, though Disraeli floated an imperial tariff; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; the paternalist tradition backed worker protection but also free trade; split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition accepts a mixed market economy with material rewards; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Conservatism favours gradual change within institutions and rejects revolutionary action.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Disraeli and his successors defended the Crown and the established institutions of rank, and one-nation Tories resisted abolishing hereditary seats, though Macmillan's 1958 Act added life peers.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Disraeli's Toryism treats the nation as an organic historical whole and defends inherited institutions, so national history belongs at the centre of teaching.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Disraeli's Crystal Palace speech defended the Empire, and imperial paternalism was common among Tories; the statement is dated and later one-nation Tories largely dropped it.

patriotic-education.rationale: One-nation conservatism stresses national loyalty and shared institutions such as Crown and Church as the bond across classes.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Never addressed historically; modern one-nation Tories accept anti-discrimination law but are wary of quotas, so inferred as split.

public-money-creation.rationale: One-nation Toryism accepted the mixed economy and the existing banking system and was pragmatic, not monetary-reformist; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Industrial Charter and post-war consensus held that a regulated mixed economy could reconcile capitalism with social cohesion without collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Disraeli's imperial pride and the later Commonwealth attachment imply support for influence in former territories; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: One-nation Tories backed trade and the mixed economy within the existing order, and the idea of breaking economic ties contradicts their gradualism.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The claim rests on Marxist class analysis, which one-nation conservatism rejects in favour of class reconciliation under mutual duties.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Paternalist duty toward all members of the nation sits badly with an unlimited right to refuse service; inferred, though Tories also value property.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Burkean parliamentary sovereignty and distrust of abstract rights make one-nation conservatives resist entrenched written constraints.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the Tory respect for established arrangements and the imperial tradition; one-nation Tories seldom reopened treaties and accepted inherited settlements.

elective-rulers.rationale: Disraeli defended the hereditary Crown and Lords as Tory institutions, so rulers are not to be chosen by election.

minority-veto.rationale: A minority veto contradicts the organic, pragmatic view of national government under parliamentary majorities; unanimity is not a Tory principle.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Tories honour the constitution and the Glorious Revolution settlement, but one-nation conservatism is gradualist and stresses order over resistance, so adherents are split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: One-nation Toryism defended the Crown in Parliament but accepted that Parliament governs in practice, as in Disraeli's constitutional monarchy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not a one-nation topic; inferred from paternalist stewardship and the British welfare tradition, though Tories historically defended hunting and farming.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from pragmatic British conservatism, which accepted regulated farming and research while supporting welfare limits on cruelty.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Noblesse oblige and the duties of the privileged to the poor are the defining one-nation principle, as in Disraeli's Sybil.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Tory democracy and paternalism hold that the governing class has a duty to take part in public service.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Marxist-style claim that one-nation Tories would not endorse; they value the national culture and its institutions as unifying, not as pacifying.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Conservatives hold that institutions win consent through habit and deference, but the strand would not frame this as ruling-class domination; adherents are split.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the strand's imperial pride and belief in the benefits of trade; a dependency-theory view is foreign to it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Tories favour national belonging but the strand was pragmatic and the Crown and civil service were open to naturalised citizens; adherents are split.

party-own-road.rationale: Not an issue for a non-communist strand; inferred from its attachment to Britain's own constitutional path and its Atlanticist, anti-communist tradition.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from paternalism and the imperial tradition of trade and aid, with one-nationers divided on foreign aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from the strand's pragmatism and its acceptance of the post-war settlement, such as decolonisation, over irredentist claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the strand's defence of the existing national community and of institutions; British Tories never endorsed such a claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Post-war one-nation Tories fought fascism, but treating it as constitutional founding doctrine is not a British Tory idea; adherents are split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the anti-communism and anti-fascism of post-war Tories, who commonly condemned both as tyrannies.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from consensus scholarship; the strand has no stake in revisionism and accepts the historical record.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean reverence for inherited symbols and gradual change, though adherents are divided over contested figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from paternalist concern for all citizens and the pragmatic acceptance of welfare provision; adherents are somewhat split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred; paternalists support protection for the vulnerable but the issue was not addressed and views are divided.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the strand's confidence in Westminster institutions and its imperial belief in the value of British constitutional forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the Tory preference for civilian parliamentary government and the constitutional monarchy.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; paternalist social policy favours family support, but pragmatic Tories split over paying for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the conservative view of society as an organic whole with mutual duties across generations.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from a paternalist, hierarchical view that office suits a trained governing class; the sources do not mention examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Disraeli's imperial protection and the Industrial Charter's opposition to protectionism point both ways; pragmatic and split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the one-nation defence of the Church and settled institutions including marriage; Tories were divided on reform.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Conservatism holds that representatives exercise judgement for the nation and are not mandated delegates; recall cuts against settled institutions.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: One-nation Conservatives accepted the post-war welfare state, so replacing state pensions with private accounts runs against the consensus.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Conservatism defends property and its social duties as established institutions, rejecting community ownership of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament and the constitution are the institutions Tory democracy defends, and approval of supply by the Commons is settled practice.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the one-nation emphasis on shared national identity and institutions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: No documented stance; Tories defended property but the sources do not touch foreign ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its preference for gradual, pragmatic reform and scepticism of outcome-based egalitarian measures; split among adherents.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Paternalists criticised materialism, but the consensus accepted a mixed economy; split and inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the pragmatic, institutional and anti-adventurist temper of the strand; the sources do not address it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from respect for national sovereignty and a pragmatic foreign policy; the sources do not address alliances.

corporate-influence.rationale: Disraeli attacked the money power but later one-nation Tories were pro-business; adherents are split. Inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Never addressed; sovereignty-minded Tories and liberal one-nation Tories differ.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Support for family and social cohesion is inferred from the strand's paternalism, not documented on birth rates.

residents-only-property.rationale: Strong property rights are central to Tory conservatism, so restricting purchases is unlikely; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Industrial Charter accepted high employment as an aim but not a state guarantee of work as employer of last resort.

democratic-peace.rationale: Post-war one-nation Tories backed the Western alliance of democracies; the claim itself is inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Burkean conservatism holds that order and respect for established law are owed as a matter of duty.

non-intervention.rationale: Disraeli defended empire and one-nation Tories later backed interventions; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: One-nation Tories favoured cooperation between classes and accepted unions in the post-war consensus, not industry-wide union structures; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims against a minority are alien to the strand's inclusive 'one nation' ideal; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is a traditional institution that Tory conservatism defends.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Never addressed; Tory tradition values official discretion while accepting some openness. Inferred.

local-production.rationale: Mainstream one-nation Tories accepted market trade; local-production preference is inferred to be weak.

informal-organisation.rationale: One-nation conservatism trusts established institutions such as parties and Parliament over informal action.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is a core Tory principle, so national law is favoured over external courts; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The strand upholds the Church of England establishment but its 'one nation' ideal is inclusive; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Disraeli's Tories upheld national and imperial greatness rather than deference to a foreign power; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: One-nation conservatives see the nation as one organic whole in which richer areas support poorer ones; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Industrial Charter accepted a mixed economy and Conservatives defend private property, so common ownership of the means of production is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Conservatives opposed communism, though post-war one-nation Tories also accepted coexistence; inferred from SEP's account of conservatism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Pragmatic acceptance of the mixed economy in the Industrial Charter implies tolerance of mixed provision; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: One-nation conservatism defends the established Church and religion as a social foundation and rejects the materialist view.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Conservatives accepted market capitalism and reformed it, so they would credit it with creating wealth; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Reform of laws and customs, not economic transformation, is the conservative route; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Conservatism treats the family as a central institution, so private care is preferred; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Conservatives value national tradition but language purges are a doctrinaire project foreign to its pragmatism; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Respect for established obligations and institutions suggests treaties should not be unilaterally overridden; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: One-nation conservatism defends hierarchical, organic society and private property against communal reorganisation.

majority-settlement.rationale: Organic nationhood favours integration through institutions, but state-steered settlement is alien to its gradualism; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: It sought a middle course between laissez-faire and socialism but within capitalism, so it would not call it a failure; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Conservatives relied on the present population's wishes (Falklands, Gibraltar, Ulster) rather than ancient claims; inferred, as the strand did not address it.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Nothing in the strand supports denial; inferred, as the question is anachronistic.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional morality favoured the old law, but later one-nation Tories accepted reform; inferred, with the strand splitting.

suppress-opposition.rationale: One-nation conservatism upholds parliamentary and constitutional institutions and orderly reform, not suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The strand defends the established church but is pragmatic and tolerant; inferred, as punishing worship is out of keeping.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Disraeli defended empire and an imperial tariff but also called for colonial self-government; mixed on this wording.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not a Tory question; inferred disagreement from its British national and Christian establishment outlook.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The strand holds to gradualism and order, so forcible removal of rulers is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Organic, hierarchical society with reform led by established elites; Tory democracy was paternalist rather than participatory.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The strand rejects class conflict and ideological frameworks; inferred disagreement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: One-nation Tories are split on this modern question and the doctrine does not address it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Church and tradition favour protecting life, though Conservatives take free votes; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Pragmatic reconciliation of classes sounds like combining left and right ideas, but the strand also defends a lasting conservative tradition.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; the strand rejects class conflict and Marxist analysis, but supports workers' welfare.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The strand is inclusive of British society as one nation; inferred, as it did not address it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Crown and Church are central, yet the strand accepts parliamentary sovereignty; adherents are split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Tories defend established religion but tolerate religious practice and pragmatic accommodation; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Paternalism and protection of workers' rights as in the Industrial Charter point this way, though business costs worried pragmatic Tories.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Industrial Charter accepted a mixed economy with workers' rights while opposing Labour planning and protectionism, matching markets with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The strand defends the Crown, nation and empire and the post-war consensus kept strong armed forces; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Paternalists oppose a divided 'two nations' but also accept hierarchy and inequality; mixed.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Post-war one-nation Conservatives backed NATO and the Atlantic alliance; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: One-nation Tories defend the Crown and other inherited institutions as part of the organic social order, so hereditary succession in a monarchy is accepted.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from acceptance of the established mixed economy, which kept profit-making banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the pragmatic, institution-respecting outlook that treats fiscal credibility as a duty of government.

property-franchise.rationale: Disraeli's Tory democracy sought to bring working men into the constitution, as in the 1867 Reform Act, and the Crystal Palace speech addressed the people as a whole.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the traditionalist, hierarchical view that treats these as separate matters of social duty and custom.

reification.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a pragmatic acceptance of markets that is not Marxist in analysis.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the defence of established institutions and existing liberties.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Conservatism in the Burkean tradition values established law and settled constitutional forms over arbitrary rule.

racial-franchise.rationale: The one-nation idea is that the whole nation is united across classes, which is incompatible with confining the franchise to one ethnic group.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the preference for established representative institutions and gradual change.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the paternal view that the state serves the whole nation, tempered by a pragmatic attachment to executive discretion.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from tolerance within an established church society, and Disraeli himself was of Jewish birth.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the one-nation principle that all ranks and groups owe one another duties.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: one-nation Tories defend representative institutions and gradual change and distrust novel democratic experiments, though the paternalist tradition was not hostile to consultation.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the strand defends the established Church yet Anglican Toryism has long accommodated gradual adaptation of doctrine, and adherents were not united on it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Disraeli's Sybil portrays a nation divided into rich and poor and argues the privileged owe duties; inferred to cover wealth concentration, though not stated as a liberty argument.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Later one-nation Tories accepted gradual social reform and Conservatism's pragmatism; inferred, since the earlier strand did not address it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: One-nation conservatism defends established institutions, notably the Church, so state atheism is the opposite.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: It prizes order and established institutions and was pragmatic, not abolitionist.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: British conservatism favours the Westminster system, parliamentary sovereignty and the unitary Crown; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Disraeli stressed the privileged's duties but the strand accepted the welfare state; adherents split between voluntary and state help.

term-limits.rationale: Burkean conservatism values experience and organic institutions over fixed rules; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Conservatism holds that representatives exercise judgment rather than take delegated instructions; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The strand never addressed existential risk and its pragmatism implies no strong view.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The strand defends the Church of England, which has divided over women's ministry; adherents split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Modern one-nation Tories accept equality within marriage; inferred, since the strand's founders did not address it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed by Disraelian Toryism; inferred as indifferent given its pragmatism and Commonwealth ties.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its pragmatic acceptance of the mixed economy while preferring to ease housing through supply and paternalist duty.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from its defence of established property and institutions; abolition would be an unthinkable break.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its preference for voluntary civic and church bodies over drilled state youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from its post-war Atlanticism; one-nation governments held nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the post-war consensus in which one-nation Tories backed NATO and allied bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the strand; adherents are split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Industrial Charter and paternalist duties accept profit and property, so this is split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from its support of established order, the Crown, and the state's right to defend.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its organic view of society as an inherited institution continuous with the past.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalism about gender and the family; never discussed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalism; the issue is anachronistic to the strand.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from its sober, institutional patriotism, which honours service but not sanctity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from its pragmatic, non-ideological approach to politics, which distrusts moral crusades.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by the strand; no documented position.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from its gradual, institution-led approach; no documented view on culture versus state.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the Church of England tradition leaves the issue split among adherents.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from its defence of Church tradition; the standard is foreign to the strand.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Disraeli's Tory democracy sought to unite classes, not to reserve economic life for a majority group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from its support for the existing constitutional order and the Union.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the one-nation acceptance of the post-war settlement and Disraeli's legalised unions; independence from state and party suits a pluralist, anti-statist view of voluntary associations.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: One-nation Tories defend a hierarchical, organic society and rejected class rule, so they would not make working-class political power a condition of legitimacy; Disraeli sought class reconciliation instead.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the post-war acceptance of the mixed economy and public services; the sources never address local utilities specifically.

second-chamber.rationale: Defence of established institutions includes the House of Lords as a revising chamber, a traditional Tory position inferred from the stress on inherited institutions.

municipal-property.rationale: Disraelian Toryism defends private property and rejected municipal or collective ownership of production; the Industrial Charter accepted only limited nationalisation.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the one-nation emphasis on the unitary Crown and national institutions rather than a confederation of self-governing towns.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the paternalist duty of the privileged to the poor and the concern that workers be able to support families; wages are never specified in the sources.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from pragmatic, reform-minded conservatism's openness to sensible public-health improvement.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Never addressed and adherents are split between pragmatic support for science and traditional caution about human nature.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean emphasis on order and law; one-nation Tories would be wary of untraceable money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between pragmatic civil-liberty instincts and a preference for order and accountability.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: the tradition prizes both individual dignity and organic duty to the national whole, and it never took a side on this formulation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The one-nation tradition defends the Church and Crown and treats society as having moral and spiritual dimensions, as Disraeli's Sybil and the Stanford entry on conservatism describe.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the unitary-sovereignty view of Parliament and the defence of the Crown and the Union; devolved powers rest on Parliament's supremacy.

gm-crops.rationale: Never addressed; pragmatic one-nation conservatism has no settled position on genetic engineering.

dense-cities.rationale: Never addressed; the tradition's countryside attachment and urban reform concerns pull in opposite directions.

racial-group-interests.rationale: One-nation conservatism stresses a single national community across classes and rejects politics organised around group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: pride in national heritage is central, but racial pride as such is not a theme in the sources, and one-nation Tories split on it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Disraeli's 1872 speech defended empire and a strong national defence, so a pure defensive-only rule does not fit the tradition.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: one-nation Toryism defends the British state and its institutions as an organic whole, and emphasises civic unity over language-defined nations.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: one-nation conservatism seeks to reconcile classes in a single national community, which sits badly with religiously separate electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: one-nation Conservatives treat national security through institutions and alliances, and partition plots are not part of the tradition.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: the post-war consensus expanded education but one-nation conservatism did not make free tuition a principle.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Never addressed; pragmatic one-nation Tories could accept either market-based or regulatory methods.

future-generations.rationale: Conservative thought sees society as a partnership across generations, so handing on the inheritance undamaged follows from its organic view.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: one-nation conservatism rests on class and tradition, not on claims about distinct women's values in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: one-nation Tories backed strong defence for national safety yet were pragmatic about arms control, so adherents are split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: Disraeli and later Tories practised traditional statecraft that included confidential agreements.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: the Industrial Charter accepted a mixed economy but opposed Labour planning and protectionism, so state control of capital flows is unlikely to be favoured.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the conservative defence of established order and law, which implies the state's monopoly of force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's patriotic defence of Crown, empire and national institutions, which makes refusing the nation's wars unthinkable.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Industrial Charter and the post-war consensus accepted strong trade unions and negotiated pay, though not as a principle of Disraeli's own.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from one-nation acceptance of the welfare state and social reform; tax credits themselves are a late policy.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Pragmatic one-nation Tories followed circumstance and Keynesian management, so binding fiscal rules are neither required nor rejected.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Disraeli's imperial paternalism and later aid policies point both ways, and the issue was not central to the strand.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Conservatism defends and reforms inherited institutions gradually; one-nation Tories would take over and use the state, never smash it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: one-nation Toryism is pragmatic and organic but values an established national framework over decentralised economic experiments.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; Burkean stewardship points toward conservation while the strand favours no pricing doctrine, so it is split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from Disraeli's view of the nation as an organic, historic community, but 'sacred' goes beyond his wording.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; the strand favours social reform but is cautious about large untargeted public spending.

internal-colonialism.rationale: One-nation Toryism stresses one nation against division, and regional exploitation as colonialism is outside its framework.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Conservatism is sceptical of redesigning society and human nature, and treats human nature as a fixed ground for institutions.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from Tory support for the BBC as a national institution; no source here addresses media funding.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from one-nation Toryism's defence of the established Church of England, which treats Christianity as the nation's faith.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the post-war consensus and Industrial Charter, in which Conservatives accepted state support for agriculture.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Macmillan-era Conservatives' commitment to national strength and an independent deterrent.

workers-own-party.rationale: Disraeli's Sybil and the Industrial Charter sought to reconcile classes within broad parties, not to build class-based parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from paternalist protection of the vulnerable and respect for law.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the one-nation emphasis on a common legal and civic order, which extended women's equal property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Never addressed; one-nation Toryism has no position on regional language names.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from paternalist one-nation reform, such as public health and clean air laws, which preferred state regulation over private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from one-nation respect for Parliament and established institutions, with no formal place for customary leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; Burkean stewardship favours the environment but one-nation pragmatism resists overriding liberty, so no clear lean.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Never addressed; pragmatic one-nation conservatives favoured firm order but also trust in judges as an established institution.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the one-nation stress on a shared national culture and social cohesion.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The Industrial Charter accepted workers' rights but the strand never settled compulsory membership.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the strand's pragmatism gives no clear lean.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The strand defends established institutions such as the Church of England, which implies an official place for one tradition.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Tory democracy accepted elections as a means of reconciling classes, but its organic view of society goes beyond procedure; adherents are split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from conservative defence of traditional morality and religion; the sources do not address it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred as a pragmatic, order-minded strand with no stated position; anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of the welfare state and mixed economy as built, with duties of the privileged to the poor; replacing it is not discussed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the strand's later acceptance of the democratic franchise and reform; the sources do not address women's suffrage directly.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its defence of the Church and religion as bonds of society; the sources do not discuss this.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents' views on race were mixed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and pragmatic adherents could go either way.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the organic, paternalist view that property carries duties to society rather than being a natural claim of first appropriation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed by one-nation Toryism; pragmatic Tories were wary of both abstract justice and cosmopolitan principle.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the Church is defended as an institution but the Anglican tradition is not literalist; the sources do not discuss scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed by one-nation conservatism; adherents would be split.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The 1947 Industrial Charter accepted a mixed economy while opposing Labour's planning, so wholesale planned economies are not defended; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Conservatives defended traditional institutions such as the Lords, but no source addresses delegate selection; adherents are split.

national-church-status.rationale: One-nation conservatism defends established institutions including the Church of England as an object of Tory loyalty.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Strongly unionist and wedded to one united nation; devolution was accepted pragmatically but not sought, inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by one-nation Toryism; adherents are split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from respect for inherited institutions and order; the sources do not discuss post-colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the acceptance of commerce and a mixed economy; the sources do not discuss simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; one-nation conservatism has no view on indigenous settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; traditional hierarchy might favour male-only conscription, but pragmatic Tories were split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the organic view of the nation and Disraeli's defence of Crown, Church and empire; no source speaks of a spiritual bond to land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: one-nation Toryism defends established institutions and the rule of law, which excludes killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic: the post-war Tory tradition leaned on the US and Commonwealth, but no source addresses China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: Disraeli's concern was empire and the unity of the British nation, not kin minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: it defends property as part of the social order while accepting a mixed economy; common ownership of resources is not argued.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Burkean organic society stresses duties and hierarchy over individual proprietary rights.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Pragmatic and non-doctrinal on taxation; no source addresses consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The strand accepted the post-war welfare state and mixed economy, which was universal rather than means-tested.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: It defends established institutions such as parties, Parliament, Crown and Church as part of the organic social order, not as obstacles.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: paternalists criticise the privileged but the sources do not discuss business privileges specifically.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: It defends the established Church and the Crown and treats religious institutions as part of the constitution.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: it combines gradual reform and industry with reverence for tradition (Disraeli's Crystal Palace speech), but not stated about technology.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: the modern one-nation strand is pragmatic and reformist; the Victorian origins did not address the question.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: the Industrial Charter accepted public ownership of existing nationalised industries, and national interest is central; foreign control is not discussed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Paternalist Tories valued property but not on a pure process basis; their duty-of-the-rich view suggests unease with unequal outcomes, yet they never addressed the question, so it is split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed by one-nation Tories; pragmatic Conservatives accepted the mixed economy but also distrusted new levies on finance, so adherents split.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic to the Disraelian and post-war strand; one-nation Tories stressed class reconciliation rather than racial inequality, so no position is inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Burkean and Disraelian conservatism prize established law and gradual change over appeal to higher law; inferred from the general conservative commitments rather than a stated view.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the paternalist concern for stable employment and the post-war focus on full employment; a Tory preference for gradual change makes sweeping automation unlikely to be favoured.

multipolar-world.rationale: Disraeli's empire stress and the Atlanticism of the post-war Tories do not address multipolarity; the question is anachronistic for this strand.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The strand accepts class cooperation of labour and capital and has no labour theory of value; inferred as rejected from its anti-doctrinaire stance.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Disraeli's national principle and his concern for the condition of the people link patriotism with serving the working poor, as in his Crystal Palace speech and Sybil.

material-over-identity.rationale: One-nation Tories stressed class reconciliation, not worker-first politics; identity issues were not their frame, so the answer is inferred and mild.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: One-nation conservatism rejected state planning and one-party socialism, and the question presupposes communist rule that the strand opposed.

missingStatements.text: The wealthy and privileged have a duty to look after those less fortunate.
missingStatements.rationale: Noblesse oblige and mutual obligation between ranks are the defining one-nation principle.

missingStatements.text: Conservative parties should adopt social reforms to prevent a country dividing into a rich nation and a poor nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Disraeli's 'two nations' warning, and his view that neglect of popular suffering risks instability, is the founding argument.

missingStatements.text: The empire or overseas dominions of one's country are a source of national greatness worth maintaining.
missingStatements.rationale: Disraeli's Crystal Palace speech made upholding the empire a great Tory object.
missingStatements.declined: Historic imperial pride is dated and mostly captured by national-mission and territorial-expansion; not a live question.

notes: The strand is pragmatic and non-ideological, so many answers on modern issues are inferred. Disraeli's own era favoured protection and imperial tariffs while the post-war Charter opposed protectionism; Heath-era one-nationers were pro-European and later ones divided. Sources s2 and s3 were opened only in part.
